tile_text: Google Lens API powers shoppable fashion content
Visual search matches outfits to product catalog
Progressive disclosure UX guides users through looks

page_copy.pattern: Fashion lookbooks create desire but traditional formats create friction between inspiration and purchase—users see outfits they love but must manually search for similar items across multiple retailers. Google Lens API offered an opportunity to bridge this gap through computer vision, automatically matching fashion photography to shoppable products. The challenge was integrating this technology into a magazine-style editorial layout without disrupting the visual experience or making the commerce aspect feel transactional rather than inspirational.
page_copy.action: Developed a custom HTML/CSS/JS fashion lookbook that integrates Google Lens API for visual search functionality, enabling users to identify and purchase items directly from editorial photography. The magazine-style layout uses progressive disclosure patterns—users can enjoy the editorial experience first, then reveal shoppable product matches through intuitive interactions. Built a multi-section architecture that handles complex navigation between different archetypal character journeys and art historical movements while maintaining conversion-focused pathways to product pages. The integration balances editorial storytelling with e-commerce functionality, keeping the primary experience inspirational while making purchase options readily accessible.
page_copy.measured: Successfully merged editorial fashion content with e-commerce functionality through computer vision technology, demonstrating capability to integrate advanced APIs into consumer-facing interfaces. The Google Lens integration reduces friction in the inspiration-to-purchase journey by automatically matching outfits to products, eliminating manual search steps. The progressive disclosure UX maintains the magazine experience while providing clear pathways to conversion when users are ready to purchase. The project showcases both technical integration skills and understanding of fashion e-commerce conversion psychology.
